transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

I... well, my husband wanted me to come. I've been... hearing things at work. I'm a mechanic, and lately, I keep hearing this man's voice. It comes from the garage vents, sometimes even from under the hood of the cars I'm working on. It's... it's as clear as if someone is standing right next to me. He keeps telling me... not to trust my husband. And he tells me not to touch certain cars. So... I'm here.
When did you first start hearing this voice? Was it sudden, or did it develop gradually over days or weeks?
I don't really know if it was sudden. It's just... it's been happening for about ten months now. The voice, and... the tracking stuff. Just about ten months.
When you think back to ten months ago, did the voice and the tracking start all at once, or did they begin very gradually over several weeks before you really noticed them?
I... I don't really remember. It's hard to think back that far. It just... it started, and now it's here.

When you hear this voice telling you not to trust your husband or not to touch certain cars, do you believe the voice is real and actually coming from outside, or do you think it might be something your mind is creating?

I... I know what I hear. It's real. The voice... it's a man's voice. Like I said, it comes from the vents. Or under the hood. It's... it's right there. Like you're sitting there. He tells me not to trust my husband. And... not to touch the cars. It's real.

If I told you that I checked the garage vents and the cars myself and found no one there, and that no one else at work has heard this voice—what would you think about that? Would it change your mind about whether the voice is real?

I... I don't really know what to tell you. Just because you didn't see anyone... doesn't mean he isn't there. 

He's... he's talking to me. Not you. Or the other guys at the shop. So... no. I guess it wouldn't change my mind. I know what I hear.

Besides hearing the voice and worrying about the tracking, how has your ability to work and take care of things at home been? Are you still able to do your job as a mechanic, or has this made it difficult for you to work?

It's... it's been hard. At the shop, I... I messed up a few times. They actually pulled me off the high-voltage EV stuff. Said they were worried I wasn't being safe. And at home... things aren't good. We fight a lot. It got so bad that... that's why my husband brought me in. For that emergency evaluation. He just... he wouldn't let it go.

Besides the voice and the tracking concerns, have you noticed any changes in how you think overall—like difficulty concentrating, your thoughts feeling jumbled or racing, or things just not making sense the way they used to?
I don't know... I mean, I guess it's hard to focus sometimes. With everything going on. But... no, my thoughts aren't racing or anything. Just... normal, I guess. I just have a lot on my mind.

Over these past ten months, have you noticed that you feel less interested in things you used to enjoy, or that you just don't feel much emotion—like you're kind of flat or numb inside, even when things happen that should make you feel something?

I don't know... maybe. There are stretches, I guess. Where I just... don't call anyone back. I used to help run the church potlucks, but I skip them now. 

Sometimes I just... sit in the house. Or in my bay at the shop, just staring at my tools. It's like I... I just can't make myself care about any of it. So... yeah.

In the past ten months, have you had any periods where you felt unusually energetic, upbeat, or 'on top of the world'—maybe needing less sleep than usual, or feeling like you could do a lot more than you normally can?

Yeah, I guess. Sometimes I get... really going. 

I'll stay late at the shop, after everyone leaves. I'll start working on three different cars at once. And then I'll start planning out a car club meet-up, or... or I'll just start reorganizing all the parts shelves. I just... I don't know, I just have to keep moving.

During those times when you're really going and staying late at the shop working on multiple cars—do you find that you need less sleep than usual, or can you get by on just a few hours and still feel rested and energized?

Yeah, I guess so. 

Like... for weeks at a time, I'd only sleep maybe two or three hours. I'd wake up before the sun was even up, and my head would already be at the shop, thinking about what I needed to do. 

It just felt like... if I tried to sleep more, I was just wasting time.

When you think back to ten months ago, before you started hearing the voice and feeling like you were being tracked—were you already having those periods where you'd sleep only a few hours and stay late at the shop working on multiple cars? Or did those energetic periods start around the same time as the voice, or after?

They were... at the same time. 

When I was staying up all night, working on everything at once... that's when the voice was coming from the vents. And... I just knew the chargers and the cameras were watching me. It all just happened together.

During those weeks when you were sleeping only 2-3 hours and working on multiple cars at the shop—did you feel like your mood was elevated or unusually good, or did you just feel driven to work without necessarily feeling happy or in a great mood?

I guess... a bit of both. 

I felt good. Like I was flying high... like I could fix every car in town. But... I don't know. It wasn't always good. 

If my husband asked why the dishes weren't done, or... if one of the techs moved my socket set... I'd just blow up at them. It just felt like they were trying to hold me down.
